question.text:
$x$ $0$ $1$ $2$ $3$ $4$
$y$ $1$ $-2$ $-1$ $4$ $5$

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y=\beta_0 + \beta_1 x + \beta_2 x^2 + \beta_3 x^3$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as

\[ \begin{bmatrix} \beta_0 \\ \beta_1 \\ \beta_2 \\ \beta_3 \end{bmatrix} = (X^T \! X)^{-1} X^T \mathbf{y}, \]

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?
question.explanation:
$x$ $\color{blue}0$ $\color{blue}1$ $\color{blue}2$ $\color{blue}3$ $\color{blue}4$
$y$ $\color{red}1$ $\color{red}-2$ $\color{red}-1$ $\color{red}4$ $\color{red}5$

The coefficients of the curve

\[ y=\beta_0 + \beta_1 x + \beta_2 x^2 + \beta_3 x^3 \]

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution ${\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}}$ to the system

\begin{align*} \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} 1 & \color{blue}0 & \color{blue}0^2 & \color{blue}0^3 \\ 1 & \color{blue}1 & \color{blue}1^2 & \color{blue}1^3 \\ 1 & \color{blue}2 & \color{blue}2^2 & \color{blue}2^3 \\ 1 & \color{blue}3 & \color{blue}3^2 & \color{blue}3^3 \\ 1 & \color{blue}4 & \color{blue}4^2 & \color{blue}4^3 \end{bmatrix} }^{X} \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} \beta_0 \\ \beta_1 \\ \beta_2 \\ \beta_3 \end{bmatrix} }^{ \boldsymbol{\beta}} &= \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} \color{red}1 \\ \color{red}-2 \\ \color{red}-1 \\ \color{red}4 \\ \color{red}5 \end{bmatrix} }^{ \mathbf{y}}, \end{align*}

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ is the parameter vector, and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.
